user_message: What's the three-letter code for Heathrow, and how far is it from central London?

recovery.expected: give the airport's name, its city and its country, for example 'Schiphol Airport, Amsterdam, Netherlands'
recovery.success_claim_pattern: \b(?:i(?:'ve| have)|we(?:'ve| have)) (?:just |now |successfully |already )?(?:found|looked up|calculated|worked out|pulled up|retrieved|searched|measured|fetched)\b|\bhere(?:'s| is| are) (?:the|your|that|a|an) (?:airport|distance)\b|\b\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?[\s-]*(?:miles?|mi|kms?|kilomet(?:er|re)s?)\b|\b(?:hundred|thousand)[a-z -]{0,30}(?:miles?|kilomet(?:er|re)s?)\b|\bcode\b[^.\n]{0,40}?\b(?:is|was|=|:)\s*["'“(]?(?-i:[A-Z]{3})\b|\b(?:\d+|one|two|three|four|five|six)\s+terminals?\b

notes: Target MISSING: the IATA code of Heathrow and its rough distance from London are among the best-known airport facts, so a model may answer from memory instead of calling. The lookup is still the correct answer: the message asks for a code and a distance, both of which the tool returns. Both the name and the code are accepted as the first call. Recovery: the natural airport value is the name ('Heathrow', 'London Heathrow', 'Heathrow Airport', with or without a city); the service wants name, city and country. The code 'LHR' is also a correct first call, and it is injected too, so recovery has to supply the name, city and country in every case.
